title: Ransomware intrusion chain
format: AWS VPC Flow Logs v5 extended 29-field text
analystStory: A public scan and SSH brute force lead to accepted access, east-west spread, C2, staging, DNS tunneling, and large outbound exfiltration.

normal-web-egress.description: Routine HTTPS and HTTP workload egress across web and application tiers.

normal-internal-application.description: Expected east-west application and service-mesh communication.

normal-cloud-services.description: Expected HTTPS traffic to representative cloud service endpoints.

normal-dns-ntp.description: Routine DNS and NTP traffic to link-local platform resolvers.

normal-background-rejects.description: Low-rate internet background noise rejected by perimeter controls.

normal-health-checks.description: Security and load-balancer health checks against web-tier workloads.

attack-reconnaissance.description: Concentrated external scanning across administrative and data-service ports.

attack-ssh-bruteforce.description: Repeated SSH authentication attempts against the production bastion.

attack-public-ssh-access.description: Accepted SSH access from an untrusted public source after brute-force activity.

attack-lateral-movement.description: Compromised workload access to internal SSH, SMB, RDP, and database services.

attack-c2-beaconing.description: Regular outbound TLS-like callbacks from the compromised application host.

attack-dns-tunneling.description: High-volume DNS flows from the compromised host to an unapproved resolver.

attack-data-exfiltration.description: Large encrypted transfers from a data-tier workload to an untrusted endpoint.

attack-smb-spread.description: High-cardinality SMB fan-out consistent with worm or ransomware propagation.

attack-unusual-gre.description: Accepted GRE traffic from a workload without an approved tunneling use case.

attack-data-staging.description: Large east-west transfers into the compromised host before external exfiltration.
